stem: Arjun knows that $8$ divides $24$ and $8$ divides $40$.

parts.text: Which claim keeps the direction of the divisibility rule straight for $24+40$ and for a split of a multiple of $8$?

options.text: $8$ divides $24+40=64$; a multiple of $8$ can still split into addends that are not both multiples of $8$.
Because $8$ divides $64$, both addends in every split of $64$ must be multiples of $8$.
$8$ divides $24+40$ when $8$ divides only one of $24$ or $40$.
The same closure also applies when different divisors act on $24$ and $40$.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: If $8$ divides both addends then $8$ divides their sum; the reverse is not forced, so a multiple of $8$ need not split into two multiples of $8$.

teacher.key_rationale: Closure: 8|24 and 8|40 ⇒ 8|64. Reverse split is not forced. B reverses. C omits both-addends condition. D changes the divisor.
